To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a reproducibility workflow is possible across all major computational biology languages and platforms, (2) the approach is flexible and can be used by researchers to produce their own reference environments, and (3) the approach is transparent and reproducible itself.

(i) a universal tool for reproducible research in computational biology does not exist; (ii) the tool we have created is a reference environment that can be used to reproduce any computational biology experiment, and (iii) the tool is not specific to a single platform, programming language, or computational paradigm.

(1) we have developed a set of tools for reproducible research that are suitable for all computational biology research, (2) we have used these tools to demonstrate reproducible research for published computational biology research papers in different areas, spanning the major computational technologies in the field, and (3) we are releasing these tools as open source, so that other researchers can use them to make their research reproducible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
reproducibility of results, not the specific implementation of those results, and our approach is not tied to any specific technology.
